name: Trophimus
overview: Trophimus was a male believer from Asia, specifically identified as being from Ephesus. His mention in the New Testament highlights his role as a companion of the Apostle Paul during his missionary journeys. Beyond his origin and faith, Scripture does not provide additional personal details about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Trophimus appears as a proper name in the New Testament. There is no specific meaning or divine origin noted for this name in the biblical text, and it is simply presented as the name of a believer associated with Paul.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Trophimus beyond his identification as a believer from Asia, particularly Ephesus. No other personal or relational details are given in the biblical record.
scriptureSignificance: Trophimus is significant in the biblical narrative as a faithful companion of Paul, representing the diverse body of believers united in Christ from various regions. His presence alongside Paul during key missionary efforts underscores the spread of the gospel beyond Jewish communities to Gentile believers. Trophimus's identification with Ephesus highlights the early Christian witness in that important city.
